newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy told by Albania three towns "out of control".
newsitem.headline: Italy told by Albania three towns "out of control".

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Wednesday he had been told by his Albanian counterpart Tritan Shehu that the situation in the southern towns of Vlore, Sarande and Delvine was "out of control".
Dini was speaking to the foreign affairs committee of the Senate (upper house) after a telephone call with Shehu in which the Albanian minister said insurgents had seized three armoured vehicles.

Dini quoted Shehu as saying that "the police and the armed forces have orders to isolate the places where rebels are concentrated, avoiding engaging in armed conflict". Shehu added that there had been no new casualties, Dini added.
Albania has imposed a state of emergency to quash an armed rebellion in the south in which some 20 people are reported to have died.

Army forces, backed by police, secured roads to the flashpoint town of Vlore on the Adriatic coast and the mountainous route between Gjirokaster and Sarande, a government information official said in Tirana earlier.

Eyewitnesses reported clashes between insurgents and army units between Sarande and Delvine, 20 km (12 miles) to the east, throughout the morning. An eyewitness said rebels had seized an army tank in Sarande and were driving it through the streets.
